title: Knowledge models carry their tenant in every key (References, corpora, categories, semantic graph)
description:
Outcome: Implements PPY-e277e3 with exact keys. KnowledgeCorpus ids become tenant-unique ("<tenant>.<corpus>"), which makes every corpus-prefixed key tenant-safe with no change (feedStateKey, starFeedKey, mediumFeedKey, contentNeededKey, publicFeedKey, corpusId indexes). Keys that are global today get "<tenant>#" in their value: Reference newsroomFeedKey ("references"), versionState, curationStatus, curationStatusKey, reviewedFeedKey, importRunId and lineageId stay as they are only if they are unique ids (importRunId, lineageId are ids: no prefix); SemanticNode newsroomFeedKey, nodeKey, versionState; SemanticRelation newsroomFeedKey ("semanticRelations"), relationTypeKey, relationDomain; SemanticRelationType key, domain, status; KnowledgeCorpus role; CategorySet status, versionState; Category status; LexicalSteeringRule status, scope; SteeringProposal status, steeringDomain; CategoryKeyword normalizedKeyword. The exact list comes from PPY-cd5926. Writers go through the tenant client (Python: records.py, reference_feed_keys.py, catalog.py, analysis_graph.py, analysis_profiles.py, assignment_executors.py; TypeScript twins under lib/, e.g. lib/reference-feed-keys.ts) so no caller builds a key by hand. Removes ReferenceIntake's refusal of tenant backends and PAPYRUS_SINGLE_PUBLICATION_BACKEND on the shared stack.

Touches (verified at origin/develop 23fabe1d): src/papyrus_content/records.py, reference_feed_keys.py (+ scripts/fixtures/reference-feed-key-vectors.json), catalog.py, monitoring_intake.py, analysis_graph.py, analysis_profiles.py, assignment_executors.py, tenancy helpers; lib/reference-feed-keys.ts, lib/tenant-keys.ts; components/topic-steering-workspace.tsx and other newsroom readers of these indexes; models Reference, ReferenceAttachment, KnowledgeCorpus, KnowledgeImportRun, KnowledgeRawPayload, KnowledgeArtifact, CategorySet, Category, CategoryKeyword, LexicalSteeringRule, SteeringProposal, SteeringDecision, SemanticNode, SemanticRelation, SemanticRelationType, CurationDelegationRecord.

Acceptance (Gherkin feature file: features_backend/tenant-knowledge-keys.feature):
Scenario: Each tenant's References page reads only its own rows
    Given 5,000 References across 50 tenants
    When "alpha" opens Predictions
    Then the index query's partition starts with an "alpha" corpus id and no other tenant's row is read

Scenario: The same feed key vectors pass in Python and TypeScript
    Given the shared vector file with tenant cases
    When both implementations run
    Then they produce the same keys

Dependencies: blocked by PPY-cd5926, PPY-94d609. Blocks PPY-bdc4ee, PPY-8f9462. (Also recorded as kbs dependencies.)
Implements or extends: PPY-e277e3.

Testing: pytest and the TypeScript vector test; call-count test (PPY-3fd0aa) at 1 and 50 tenants; Behave in a sandbox.
Rollout: Writers first (dual-read: an unprefixed key is still read for rows not yet adopted), then the backfill (PPY-8f9462), then readers drop the fallback. No new index.
Risk and mitigation: Risk: a reader still asks the unprefixed partition after the backfill and shows an empty page. Mitigation: the request meter logs every query on an unprefixed global partition on a shared stack; CI fails on it.

Releasable on its own: yes.
DynamoDB index: none.
AppSync authorisation: unchanged.
Design note: docs/plans/multi-tenant-architecture.md (PR on branch docs/multi-tenant-architecture).
